# Changing a filter drops the active sort, while the header still shows it

## Context

Found in team:engine release testing, 2026-10-20. A read-only headless sweep reproduced it 2/2 in four examples, and I reproduced it directly in `examples/grid/animatedRowSorting` (headless Chrome, dev server). The steps: type `a` in the Firstname field (7 rows, insertion order), then click the Firstname header, which sorts them ascending. Refining the field to `am` then gives Sam, William, Amanda instead of Amanda, Sam, William. Clearing the field brings back insertion order. Through all of it the header keeps its ascending arrow and `store.sorters` is unchanged.

The sweep saw the same in `examples/grid/issues` (search, sort Opened, refine the search), `examples/tableFiltering` and `examples/grid/contentSizedRows`. 13.3's header menus and search make this path routine: sort a column, then narrow by menu or search.

## The Problem

Once a filter is active, every later filter change returns the rows in the order they had when the collection was first filtered, not in sorter order. A filter whose value is `null` still counts as active, so clearing a field does not restore the sort either.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/collection/Base.mjs#filter`: the branch for no active filters re-applies the sorters (`needsSorting = true` → `me.doSort(me.items, true)`). The branch for active filters rebuilds `_items` from `evaluateFilters()` and does not.
- `evaluateFilters()` walks `this.allItems?._items`. `allItems` is created from `_items` on the first filter, and `doSort()` sorts only `_items`, so `allItems` keeps its creation-time order from then on.
- 13.2.0 has the same `filter()` shape (it also iterates `allItems._items`), so this is not a 13.3 regression.
- Design authority: `filter()` itself, which re-applies the sorters on its no-filter branch. That makes "the filtered items follow the sorters" the method's own contract, and the active-filter branch breaks it. Also the Collections guide's *Sorting Data*: "`Neo.collection.Sorter` instances are used to sort the items within a collection."

## The Fix

In `filter()`, re-apply the active sorters after either branch, whenever the collection has sorters. Keep remote sorting and `filterMode: 'primitive'` behaving as they do today.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 (unit): a sorted collection with an active filter keeps sorter order when the filter's value changes, and when it is cleared to `null`.
- [ ] AC-2 (unit): without sorters, filtering keeps today's order.
- [ ] AC-3 (e2e): in `examples/grid/animatedRowSorting`, filter `a`, sort Firstname, refine to `am`: the rows read Amanda, Sam, William. The case fails on `dev` and passes with the fix.
- [ ] AC-4: the collection, store and grid unit suites stay green.

## Out of Scope

- Keeping `allItems` itself in sorter order. Re-sorting the filtered result is enough here.
- Remote sorting and filtering.

## Related

- #19669 / #19673 (the column filters that use `evaluateFilters`), and the 13.3 header-menu and search chapters (#19712).

sorters after either branch.
